_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for WMT retrospectives (retro/build_wmt.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2008 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it; a next-quarter guide while its quarter is unreported) and the latest declared dividend. Walmart's fiscal year N ends on January 31 of calendar year N. Each release guides diluted EPS from continuing operations for the next quarter and, in most releases, the fiscal year; U.S. comparable store sales for the next quarter in most; never net sales or a margin. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest filing that reports it (the 10-K's Eleven-Year Financial Summary for EPS and net sales; the statements of income for diluted shares). A print's growth, margins and inventory growth are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', millions; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago quarter is the one the same release shows; comparable store sales are the release's Total U.S. figure with fuel, the measure the 10-Ks report. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds, with the raw figures they are computed from. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

history_vintages.why: Walmart: 'operates retail stores in various formats around the world and is committed to saving people money so they can live better'; 'every day low prices (“EDLP”)'; 'The retail business is highly competitive' (its Wal-Mart Stores segment competes with discount, department, drug, variety and specialty stores, supermarkets, supercenter-type stores and hypermarts, 'as well as internet-based retailers and catalog businesses'); and 'General economic conditions, globally or in one or more of the markets we serve, may adversely affect our financial performance' (its own FY2007 10-K): a low-price store network whose demand follows the consumer economy by its own account; no disruption theme is live for it
history_vintages.normalization: diluted income per share from continuing operations, each year from the latest 10-K that reports it (the FY2007 10-K's Eleven-Year Financial Summary, restated for the McLane, South Korea and Germany dispositions; fiscal 2000 before the cumulative effect of the Sam's Club membership accounting change); no company figure excluding a one-off is published for any year and no year's one-offs reach half its income, so no year is excluded

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'WMT'): the decade of the FY2007 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is fiscal 1998-2007 (fiscal years end January 31). Each year-on-year change comes from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years. For net sales, cost of sales, U.S. comparable store sales and inventories that is the FY2007 10-K's Eleven-Year Financial Summary (one table, restated for the McLane, South Korea and Germany dispositions; comparable store sales in whole percents as the table gives them, with the fiscal 2007 change of definition left in). The summary has no operating income, so each operating-margin change comes from the statements of income of the latest 10-K reporting both years (operating income = net sales and other income less cost of sales and operating, selling, general and administrative expenses, over net sales; a line in the statements from the FY2003 10-K, derived before it). Seams stay in, as published: the 1999-2000 Asda acquisition, the 2005-2006 Seiyu consolidation, the reclassification of interest income out of other income in the FY2003 10-K.
